job.title: Manager Community Safety
job.description:
About Strathbogie Shire Council

Strathbogie Shire Council is a progressive regional municipality encompassing communities including Euroa, Nagambie, Avenel and Violet Town, ideally positioned between Melbourne and Shepparton.

Council is committed to delivering responsive, consistent and customer focused services that support community safety, regulatory compliance and the amenity of the Shire. With a diverse rural landscape and a broad range of services, Council plays an important role in supporting residents, businesses and communities across the municipality.

This is an opportunity to build on significant service improvements, strengthen team capability and shape how community safety and regulatory services operate within a regional council, with practical opportunities to improve the experience of the community.

About the Role

Reporting to the Director Community & Planning, the Manager Community Safety will lead a diverse portfolio spanning local laws, community compliance, animal management, environmental health, building, planning compliance and emergency management.

This is a broad leadership position with responsibility for service delivery, legislative compliance, people leadership and continuous improvement across several interconnected functions. You will oversee day-to-day operations, support and develop a multidisciplinary team, manage resources and budgets, and ensure services are delivered consistently and effectively.

A key priority will be to oversee the implementation of Council’s new local law, embedding clear processes and supporting consistent application across the municipality. You will also drive practical improvements to regulatory services, including streamlining permitting processes, strengthening customer communication and identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and accessibility for residents and businesses.

You will build on work already undertaken to review services, systems and team structures, establishing clear accountabilities, effective reporting and a positive, accountable team culture. The role will also provide leadership across emergency management and recovery, supporting Council’s preparedness, response and recovery responsibilities.

Working closely with the Director, Councillors, staff, community members, businesses and external service providers, you will provide sound advice on complex regulatory matters, manage sensitive complaints and ensure legislative obligations are met. This is an opportunity to balance operational leadership with longer-term service development and make a tangible difference to how Council supports its community.
  
About You

You are an experienced regulatory services or community safety leader who brings sound judgement, strong people leadership and a practical approach to improving services. You understand the importance of balancing legislative requirements with responsive, accessible customer service, and can navigate complex matters involving competing stakeholder interests and community expectations.

You bring experience interpreting and applying legislation, developing policies and procedures, and leading change across a multidisciplinary team. You are comfortable managing operational priorities, budgets and resources while identifying opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen accountability and deliver better outcomes.

Just as importantly, you are a calm, measured and approachable leader who builds trust, sets clear expectations and supports people to perform at their best. You can have difficult conversations when required, address performance constructively and foster a culture of professionalism, collaboration and continuous improvement.

You are confident engaging with a broad range of stakeholders, from residents and local businesses through to Councillors, senior leaders and external agencies. You bring the ability to make considered decisions on sensitive issues, communicate clearly and maintain a focus on fair, consistent and defensible outcomes.

Experience across every service area is not essential, what matters is your ability to lead across a varied portfolio, apply sound judgement and build your knowledge where needed. An understanding of emergency management, business continuity and disaster recovery will be important, alongside a genuine interest in the opportunities and practical challenges of working within a rural municipality.

Most importantly, you are motivated by the opportunity to lead a broad and meaningful portfolio, build on existing improvements and help shape a capable, connected and customer focused community safety function.

About Melton City Council

Melton City Council is one of Australia’s fastest-growing municipalities, with expanding communities, new development and emerging employment precincts shaping its future.

This growth creates a significant opportunity for Council’s building services function. As the municipality evolves, the service needs the leadership, capability and systems to respond to increasing demand while protecting community safety and delivering its statutory responsibilities.

Council is seeking a Municipal Building Surveyor who wants to help shape that future. This appointment offers genuine scope to influence how the department is structured, how its people are supported and how building services are delivered across the municipality.

With senior management seeking a clearer direction for the function, and work already underway to address outstanding compliance matters, the incoming MBS will have a strong platform from which to build the next phase of the service.

About the Role

The Municipal Building Surveyor is responsible for administering Council’s statutory building functions and providing leadership, technical oversight and direction to the building services team.

Alongside these statutory responsibilities, the role offers an opportunity to shape the department’s ongoing structure and operating model. Working with senior management, you will assess the service’s needs, clarify responsibilities and identify the leadership arrangements and technical capability required to support a growing municipality.

The service’s current focus is on compliance, enforcement, inspections and Council’s broader municipal building responsibilities. Council does not currently issue building permits, with the incoming MBS expected to review the service model and provide considered advice on its future scope, including whether a municipal permit offering would be appropriate.

A key priority will be establishing a clear understanding of the team’s workload, capability and outstanding matters, then ensuring work is prioritised and delivered consistently. You will support staff to make sound decisions, provide clear technical guidance and strengthen accountability across the service.

Swimming pool and spa compliance work is also underway, with an established team progressing Council’s obligations in this area. There is scope to move the department towards a more planned and proactive approach, with clearer priorities, stronger reporting and a shared understanding of what effective service delivery looks like.

You will help translate that direction into practical changes to team structure, processes and day-to-day operations. You will also provide clear advice on complex or sensitive building matters, ensuring statutory decisions are well considered and that senior leaders understand the service’s risks, priorities and resource requirements.

About You

You are an experienced building surveyor with Unlimited registration in Victoria and the technical capability required to perform the statutory responsibilities of a Municipal Building Surveyor.

You bring strong knowledge of building legislation, compliance, enforcement and regulatory decision-making, supported by experience managing complex building matters.

You are motivated by the opportunity to build and shape a department. You can assess how a service is operating, identify the capability and structure it needs, and work with senior management and staff to turn that thinking into practical improvements.

You are a visible and engaged leader who provides clear direction, supports staff and follows through on priorities. You establish expectations while giving your team the guidance and confidence to take ownership of their work.

You are comfortable leading through change and reviewing established practices with an open mind. You will take the time to understand the team’s strengths and challenges, then set a clear direction that supports both immediate delivery and the department’s longer-term development.

Experience in local government would be valuable, alongside the ability to work collaboratively with senior leaders and provide sound advice in a municipal regulatory environment.

Most importantly, you will bring energy, sound judgement and a constructive leadership style, with the ambition to shape a capable building service that keeps pace with the Melton community.

job.title: Manager City Strategy
job.description:
About Melton City Council

Melton City Council serves a rapidly growing municipality in Melbourne’s west, where expanding communities, new employment precincts and major infrastructure investment are shaping the city’s future.

Strategic planning plays a central role in managing this growth. Council is planning for new development while responding to the needs of established communities, ensuring land use, infrastructure and community facilities support the municipality’s long-term future.

Council is seeking a Manager City Strategy to provide strategic direction and engaged leadership across a diverse portfolio. This is an opportunity to influence how Melton develops, lead a capable team and build the relationships needed to translate strategy into practical outcomes.

About the Role

The Manager City Strategy leads Council’s strategic planning, urban design and heritage, open space and community infrastructure planning, sustainability and climate resilience functions.

Strategic planning is a key priority, with a significant program of work across growth areas, emerging industrial and employment land, planning scheme amendments and major government projects. You will guide the preparation of policies and planning frameworks that establish a clear direction for future land use and development.

Current priorities include the Melton East Precinct Structure Plan and engagement with State Government projects. You will ensure Council’s interests are clearly represented and that planning advice reflects the connections between growth, infrastructure, employment and community needs.

The broader portfolio brings together functions that influence the quality and sustainability of the municipality. Urban design and heritage inform how places develop and retain their identity, while open space and community infrastructure planning help establish what growing and established communities will need into the future.

The department also develops policy and strategic direction across sustainability, climate resilience and circular economy. You will ensure these priorities are considered alongside land use and infrastructure planning, with clear frameworks that other parts of Council can use to guide their work.

A central part of the role will be bringing clarity and coordination to the department’s work program. Supported by coordinators and specialist staff, you will establish priorities, clarify responsibilities and ensure the team has the direction and support needed to deliver.

You will work closely with colleagues across Council to connect strategic planning with implementation. This requires early engagement, an understanding of operational needs and a collaborative approach to developing policies and frameworks that can be put into practice.

Beyond the organisation, you will build productive relationships with government agencies, developers, industry and community stakeholders. You will represent Council confidently, provide clear advice and help progress complex matters involving different interests and responsibilities.
  
  
About You

You bring substantial experience in strategic planning, land use or a closely related field, together with the leadership capability to guide a multidisciplinary team.

You understand the planning challenges and opportunities associated with a growing municipality. You can provide sound direction across growth area planning, planning scheme amendments and emerging land use priorities, while considering the infrastructure, environmental and community implications of those decisions.

You are an engaging and collaborative leader who takes an active interest in the team’s work. You provide clear expectations, practical guidance and the support people need to contribute confidently and take ownership of outcomes.

You can bring clarity to a broad portfolio, helping coordinators and specialists understand priorities, manage competing demands and work effectively together. You value their expertise while maintaining accountability for performance and delivery.

You build strong relationships across an organisation and understand that effective strategy depends on the involvement of the people who will implement it. You listen to different perspectives, work constructively through issues and help colleagues reach decisions that move work forward.

You are also comfortable representing Council externally, engaging with industry and government, and communicating complex planning matters clearly. You combine strategic thinking with a practical approach to getting things done.

Local government experience would be valuable, although Council is open to candidates from other relevant environments who bring strong planning expertise, effective leadership and a clear understanding of the public outcomes this work supports.

Most importantly, you will bring energy, sound judgement and a collaborative approach to leading the team and shaping Melton’s future.
